answer_text:
Let

\[
f(x)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(n-1)!}{\prod_{r=1}^{n}(x+r)},\qquad x>0.
\]

Define

\[
P_n=\prod_{r=1}^{n}(x+r),\qquad P_0=1,
\]

and

\[
T_n=\frac{n!}{P_n}.
\]

Then for \(n\ge 1\),

\[
T_{n-1}-T_n
=
\frac{(n-1)!}{P_{n-1}}-\frac{n!}{P_n}.
\]

Since \(P_n=P_{n-1}(x+n)\), we get

\[
T_{n-1}-T_n
=
\frac{(n-1)!}{P_{n-1}}-\frac{n(n-1)!}{P_{n-1}(x+n)}.
\]

Factor:

\[
T_{n-1}-T_n
=
(n-1)!P_{n-1}^{-1}
\left(1-\frac{n}{x+n}\right).
\]

But

\[
1-\frac{n}{x+n}=\frac{x}{x+n},
\]

so

\[
T_{n-1}-T_n
=
x\cdot \frac{(n-1)!}{P_{n-1}(x+n)}
=
x\cdot \frac{(n-1)!}{P_n}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\frac{(n-1)!}{\prod_{r=1}^{n}(x+r)}
=
\frac1x\left(T_{n-1}-T_n\right).
\]

Hence the series telescopes:

\[
\sum_{n=1}^{N}\frac{(n-1)!}{\prod_{r=1}^{n}(x+r)}
=
\frac1x\sum_{n=1}^{N}(T_{n-1}-T_n)
=
\frac1x(T_0-T_N).
\]

Since \(T_0=1\), we have

\[
\sum_{n=1}^{N}\frac{(n-1)!}{\prod_{r=1}^{n}(x+r)}
=
\frac1x\left(1-T_N\right).
\]

Now

\[
T_N=\frac{N!}{\prod_{r=1}^{N}(x+r)}
=
\frac{N!\,\Gamma(x+1)}{\Gamma(N+x+1)}.
\]

As \(N\to\infty\),

\[
T_N\sim \frac{\Gamma(x+1)}{N^x}\to 0
\]

because \(x>0\). Thus

\[
f(x)=\lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1x(1-T_N)=\frac1x.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac1x}
\]
